title: Automated Legacy Microservice Refactoring
business: Enterprise financial software providers maintaining massive, monolithic codebases.
problem: Engineers struggle to decompose legacy services into independent modules due to deep, undocumented dependency chains that span thousands of files, leading to high regression risks.
solution: GPT-5.2-Codex utilizes its 400,000 context window and agentic reasoning capabilities to map cross-module dependencies and propose refactoring plans by analyzing the entire repository structure simultaneously.
steps: Ingest the entire legacy repository into the context window to establish a global dependency graph.
Configure the reasoning effort to xhigh to allow the model to simulate the impact of code changes across disparate modules.
Utilize the Responses API with function_calling to execute targeted refactoring scripts within a hosted_shell environment.
Validate the proposed module separation using the model's ability to generate unit tests for the newly isolated components.
outcome: A modularized architecture where individual services can be updated or deployed independently without triggering cascading failures in the legacy core.
limitation: The model may hallucinate dependency relationships if the codebase contains highly obfuscated or non-standard patterns; verify by checking the generated dependency graph against static analysis tools.
